source.description: Vectors for the zkgroup credential and proof half used by a groups v2 client: poksho, zkcredential, AuthCredentialWithPni (zkc), ExpiringProfileKeyCredential, group send endorsements and server notary signatures, as implemented by libsignal v0.99.1 (bundled with signal-cli v0.14.7). See spec/crypto/zkgroup-credentials.md. All hex is lowercase. Points are 32-byte RFC 9496 ristretto255 encodings; scalars are 32-byte little-endian integers reduced mod the group order; integers inside serialized structures are little-endian unless the spec says otherwise.

provenance.upstream: Fields marked kind=upstream (or listed under an upstream_* key) are copied as data from libsignal @ 97801d22: rust/poksho/src/{shosha256,sign,statement}.rs unit tests, rust/zkcredential/src/credentials.rs (hardcoded SystemParams), rust/zkgroup/src/crypto/{credentials,uid_encryption,profile_key_encryption}.rs (hardcoded SystemParams), rust/zkgroup/tests/integration_tests.rs (AUTH_CREDENTIAL_PRESENTATION_V4_RESULT, PROFILE_KEY_CREDENTIAL_PRESENTATION_V4_RESULT, EXPECTED_SIGNATURE). Every upstream zkgroup value was also reproduced byte for byte by the reference jar run described under reference_jar.
provenance.reference_jar: Computed offline by the reference distribution: jshell (JDK 25.0.5, LANG=C.UTF-8) with class path /work/third_party/signal-cli-0.14.7/lib/*.jar (libsignal-client-0.99.1.jar with its native library), no network. Randomness was injected by passing a java.security.SecureRandom subclass whose nextBytes(byte[32]) copies the listed 32 fixed bytes; every API used draws exactly one 32-byte block per call. APIs: ServerSecretParams.generate(SecureRandom), getPublicParams(), sign(SecureRandom, byte[]); ServerPublicParams.verifySignature; GroupSecretParams.deriveFromMasterKey; ServerZkAuthOperations.issueAuthCredentialWithPniZkc(SecureRandom, Aci, Pni, Instant); ClientZkAuthOperations.receiveAuthCredentialWithPniAsServiceId(Aci, Pni, long, response) and createAuthCredentialPresentation(SecureRandom, GroupSecretParams, AuthCredentialWithPni); ServerZkAuthOperations.verifyAuthCredentialPresentation; ProfileKey.getCommitment/getProfileKeyVersion; ClientZkProfileOperations.createProfileKeyCredentialRequestContext(SecureRandom, Aci, ProfileKey), receiveExpiringProfileKeyCredential(context, response, Instant), createProfileKeyCredentialPresentation(SecureRandom, GroupSecretParams, credential); ServerZkProfileOperations.issueExpiringProfileKeyCredential(SecureRandom, request, Aci, commitment, Instant) and verifyProfileKeyCredentialPresentation; ClientZkGroupCipher.encrypt; GroupSendDerivedKeyPair.forExpiration; GroupSendEndorsementsResponse.issue(List, keyPair, SecureRandom) and receive(List<ServiceId>, Aci, Instant, GroupSecretParams, ServerPublicParams) and receive(List<UuidCiphertext>, UuidCiphertext, Instant, ServerPublicParams); GroupSendEndorsement.combine/byRemoving/toToken; GroupSendEndorsement.Token.toFullToken; GroupSendFullToken.verify.
provenance.derived_by_spec_agent: Fields under 'intermediate' keys and the poksho statement descriptions were computed by the spec agent with a throwaway scratch implementation of the spec (Java BigInteger ristretto255, HMAC Sho, poksho), not delivered and deleted after the run. That implementation reproduced, byte for byte, every reference_jar output in this file (issuance-proof verification, credentials, request contexts, requests, presentations, endorsements, tokens) and every upstream poksho/Sho vector, so the intermediates are consistent with libsignal; libsignal does not expose them directly.
provenance.upstream_fixed_vectors_searched: rust/zkgroup/tests/*.rs, rust/zkgroup/src/**, rust/zkcredential/src/**, rust/poksho/src/**, java/client/src/test/java/org/signal/libsignal/zkgroup/**, node/ts/test/ZKGroup-test.ts, swift/Tests/LibSignalClientTests/ZKGroupTests.swift. The Java/Node/Swift fixed hex for this feature set are the same three integration-test results (plus obsolete V1/V2/V3 presentations, not included); GroupSendEndorsement tests use Instant.now() and have no fixed outputs.

fixed_randomness.note: TEST_ARRAY_32* as in libsignal rust/zkgroup/src/common/constants.rs; T32 = 00..1f, T32_1 = 64..83, T32_2 = c8..e7, T32_3 = 01..20, T32_4 = 02..21, T32_5 = 03..22 (consecutive byte values).

sho_sha256.steps: new(label=''); absorb_and_ratchet('abc'); absorb_and_ratchet(0x00*63); absorb_and_ratchet(0x00*64); absorb_and_ratchet(0x00*65); absorb_and_ratchet(0x00*127); absorb_and_ratchet(0x00*128); absorb_and_ratchet(0x00*129); squeeze_and_ratchet(63); squeeze_and_ratchet(64); squeeze_and_ratchet(65); squeeze_and_ratchet(127); squeeze_and_ratchet(128); squeeze_and_ratchet(129); absorb_and_ratchet('def'); squeeze_and_ratchet(63) -> output

statement_encodings.statement: A = a*G + b*H + c*I; B = c*H + d*I

complex_statement.statement: A = a*G + b*H + c*I; B = c*H + d*I
complex_statement.inputs_rule: a,b,c,d = wide reduction of the 64 bytes (k+i) for i=0..63 with k = 10,20,30,40; H = h*G and I = i*G with h,i the wide reductions for k = 50,60; message empty; randomness 00..1f

statement_descriptions.kind: derived_by_spec_agent (verified: the jar's proofs verify under these descriptions and the scratch prover reproduces the jar's client proofs)

system_params.kind: upstream (hardcoded constants; each also re-derived by the spec agent from the generation rule in the spec)
